title: Goroutines & Channels Basics
intro: Learn Go concurrency as a set of ownership and lifecycle rules, not isolated syntax. This module explains how the runtime schedules goroutines on operating-system threads, how typed channels transfer values and synchronize work, where buffered and unbuffered operations block, who owns closing, why range needs a completed stream, and how select and context make waiting cancellable. It finishes by combining channels, mutexes, WaitGroups, and context in a bounded worker pool. Every lesson includes a deterministic runnable example and a diagram or table for the relationship being taught.
